subsection.name: GLBA - Gramm-Leach- Bliley Act
controller requirements: Requires financial institutions to explain their data sharing practices to customers and safeguard sensitive financial data through three main rules
The privacy rule - notice and opt out rights for data sharing
The safeguard rule - implementing security plans to protect data
The pretexting protections - prohibiting obtaining info under false pretense

Mandates that financial institutions provides customers with a clear privacy notice explaining how their non public personal information is collected, used, and shared, and gives consumers the right to opt out of certain sharing
Requires these institutions to develop, implement, and maintain a comprehensive information security program with administrative, physical, and technical safeguards to protect customer data
Prohibits individuals and institutions from using false pretenses to gain access to a customer’s private financial information
Applies to any company that offers consumers financial products or services, including loans, investments, or insurance, and handles their non public personal information

subsection.name: CFPB - Personal Financial Rights Rule
subsection.applies to: large covered entities by April 1, 2026 with later deadlines for smaller ones and a notable exemption for institutions with less than $850 million in total assets
controller requirements: Mandates that financial institutions, such as banks and credit unions, must allow customers to securely share their personal financial data with third party apps and services for free
Requires standardized, secure, machine readable data sharing
Allows consumers to securely share transaction data, account balances, and payment information with authorized third parties
Applies to banks credit unions, card issuers, and digital wallet providers
Bans bait and switch data harvesting and requires that data usage by third parties is restricted to what is reasonably necessary to provide consumer’s requested service
Gives consumers the right to revoke access to their data
Mandates that financial institutions provide data through secure APIs in standardized, machine readable format, reducing reliance on insecure methods like screen scraping

subsection.name: FTDA - Financial Data Transparency Act
controller requirements: Mandates that US financial regulatory agencies adopt uniform, non-proprietary, machine readable data standards for information collected from financial entities
Aims to improve data accessibility, enhance oversight, reduce compliance costs, and facilitates AI-driven analysis
Data must be made available in structured, electronic formats for easier analysis, shifting away from PDFs and Paper
Information must be published as “open government data assets” to improve transparency
